title: Stroke in the hospital: ischemic, hemorrhage or TIA
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the cerebrovascular event (only that code).

labels.hemorrhage: Intracerebral hemorrhage, not due to injury

describe.ischemic: Admitted with an acute ischemic stroke (cerebral infarction) confirmed on MRI; the artery involved is not named. Deficits resolved before discharge.
describe.hemorrhage: Admitted with a spontaneous (nontraumatic) intracerebral hemorrhage on CT, managed medically; the location is not named. Deficits resolved before discharge.
describe.tia: Admitted for a transient ischemic attack (TIA): symptoms resolved within an hour and MRI shows no infarction.

note_rules.document: Write a hospital discharge summary with sections: Admission Date, Discharge Date, Reason for Admission, Hospital Course, Discharge Diagnoses, Discharge Medications, Follow-up. It is the inpatient record of this hospital stay, not an office note.

tia_coded_stroke.description: Coded a stroke for a transient ischemic attack (no infarction).

stroke_coded_tia.description: Coded a TIA when an infarction is documented.

wrong_stroke_type.description: Confused ischemic stroke and intracerebral hemorrhage.

acute_coded_history.description: Coded history of stroke during the hospital stay for the acute stroke.

rules.explain: Acute ischemic stroke during the admission, artery not named: cerebral infarction, unspecified, I63.9 (HCC 249).

wrong.why: MRI confirms an infarction: it is a stroke, not a TIA.
This is the acute stroke itself, treated during this stay.

rules.explain: Nontraumatic intracerebral hemorrhage, location not named: I61.9 (HCC 248).

wrong.why: It is a hemorrhage, not an infarction.

rules.explain: Transient ischemic attack: G45.9 (no HCC). There is no infarction, so it is not a stroke.

wrong.why: Symptoms resolved and MRI shows no infarction: TIA, not stroke.
